text:
joel: Hey - just got escalated from ACME: users signing in via SSO + MFA keep getting kicked into a reauth loop when using our embedded inference widget inside their app. Works fine if they open the widget in a new tab. Seen across Chrome and Safari.

joel: Quick repro we ran: 1) Login SSO -> complete MFA on top-level app. 2) Load page with <iframe src="https://console.redwood.ai/embed/widget">. 3) Widget redirects to /auth/reauth -> returns 302 to SSO -> user prompted again, then back to widget, repeat.

joel: We captured network and cookies: the widget requests include rw_session_v2 cookie but iframe-origin flow seems to trigger another set-cookie from our auth callback that doesn't stick. Relevant Set-Cookie header:

```
Set-Cookie: rw_session_v2=eyJ...; Path=/; Domain=.acme.com; Secure; SameSite=None; HttpOnly; Max-Age=3600
```

joel: Also noticed an Authorization: Bearer <device-trust-jwt> header present on parent app but not forwarded into iframe requests (expected). Customer claims this started after a small auth change last week.

maria: Thanks for the detailed repro. I pinged ACME to ask for HAR and a short screen capture. @ben any guesses from auth infra?

ben: Probably cookie scoping / rotation race. If the top-level app performs a rekey of the device-jwt or rotates the session cookie around the same time the embed tries to refresh, we can end up with two competing Set-Cookie flows. In iframes the browser can drop third-party cookies if SameSite or cross-site restrictions apply.

ben: A couple quick checks: 1) Confirm the embed is loaded cross-site (acme.com -> console.redwood.ai). 2) Check whether the auth callback after SSO sets a new rw_session_v2 with a different path or domain. 3) Look for a subsequent Set-Cookie that has no SameSite or SameSite=Lax which would be blocked.

acme-cs: FYI we tried altering the widget to include allow="cross-origin-embedder" — no change. We can repro consistently with a test account.

maria: Can you attach HAR? Also are you using our hosted embed (console.redwood.ai) or a self-hosted SDK?

acme-cs: Hosted embed. HAR attached in ticket (link).

ben: Looking at the HAR (thanks) I see two Set-Cookie lines within ~600ms: one from /auth/complete on console.redwood.ai and one immediately after from acme.com's IdP callback proxied through their backend. Browser ends up keeping acme.com's cookie but not the console one (third-party). That explains the repeated redirect — widget thinks session missing and triggers reauth.

ben: Short-term mitigation: have the widget open auth flow in top-level (window.top) instead of doing everything inside iframe. That preserves first-party cookie semantics. Not ideal UX but reduces reauth loops.

maria: Can we offer a safer workaround from our side? Maybe set an alternative fallback cookie name or use postMessage handshake?

ben: postMessage can work: after parent finishes SSO, parent can post the device-trust token to the iframe; widget then attaches token to Authorization header for subsequent calls, avoiding Set-Cookie entirely. Requires minor change in embed integration.

sre-oncall: Deploy bot noted a config change in auth service on 1938740000 where we updated cookie TTL handling for rw_session_v2 (diff: remove set-cookie-behavior override). @deploy-bot can you link the diff?

deploy-bot: Deployed auth-service@v2.14.3 to prod at 1938740123. Change: normalize SameSite=None on Set-Cookie for cross-site embeds.

ben: Aha — that change was intended to improve cross-site behavior but an edge-case in our proxy caused the Set-Cookie to use Domain=.acme.com (proxied IdP path) which the browser treated as cross-site third-party and dropped. Rolling forward the change without the acme domain mapping caused the race.

security: Does this create any token leakage risk if we advise customers to postMessage tokens? We should document the pattern with explicit listener checks and origin enforcement.

ben: Agreed. postMessage must validate event.origin and only accept the token from the parent domain. Also tokens we accept can be scoped short-lived and single-use to reduce risk.

maria: Next steps for support: 1) Ask ACME to temporarily change the embed to do top-level auth redirect (quick test). 2) If that fixes it, offer code snippet and migration plan for postMessage handshake and short-lived token. 3) Engineering to roll a safe fix that avoids competing Set-Cookie headers for our hosted embeds and ensure we never emit cookies with the customer's domain.

maria: Snippet suggestion for ACME (postMessage flow):

```
// parent after SSO completes
const token = "\"device-trust-token-from-backend\"";
const iframe = document.getElementById('rw-widget');
iframe.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'RW_DEVICE_TOKEN', token }, 'https://console.redwood.ai');

// widget side
window.addEventListener('message', (e) => {
  if (e.origin !== 'https://acme.com') return; // enforce
  if (e.data?.type === 'RW_DEVICE_TOKEN') {
    // attach token to future requests
  }
});
```

joel: ACME confirmed top-level auth avoids the loop. They prefer postMessage integration rather than UX change.

ben: We'll prioritize a small auth-service rollback to avoid setting rw_session_v2 cookie with the customer's domain in our auth callback for hosted embed flows. I filed ENG-5123.

security: I'll create a short doc for secure postMessage usage and token scopes. Keep me looped.

maria: I'll reply to ACME with repro confirmation, the postMessage snippet, and the temporary guidance. Marking support ticket P1 and looping in eng and security. :white_check_mark:

acme-cs: Thanks everyone, appreciate the quick turnaround. We'll implement postMessage and report back in ~2 days.

joel: updating ticket and closing this thread for now; will reopen if ACME sees recurrence.
